subject: host-effect-authorization.v3
protocol: Independent review under D-000; refute not confirm; successor to v2 (Claude 2 ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, Codex REJECT at HAE2-CX-01..03)
summary: The substantive repairs are excellent and I could falsify none of them. CA-1 replay is bound by componentGenerationIdentity and admittedManifestDigest with mismatch DENYING, plus a designContractRef whose staleness denies and for which 'Existence of this JSON on disk is not a lawful ref'. The CA-1 commit boundary is moved off parent-pid observation to OS acceptance of process creation, with an unknownAcceptance clause that covers the exact TOCTOU races. ES-2 is split so a CA-2 customer tool is no longer mis-assigned to a DR-105 component token — 'A customer tool is not made a component by being spawned' — which was a real category error in v2. The process-death gap is refused honestly rather than papered over: no surviving writer is minted, the surface is marked UNOWNED-AND-NEEDED with a D-000 owner-assignment route, and the fixture is explicitly bounded rather than claimed. One blocker stands, and it is self-declared. doctorV4FieldMapping states 'Total mapping. An authorizationRecord member with no mapped consentRecords field is a defect in this contract' — and two of the nineteen closed members have no mapping, one of them the member that carries classification.

findings.claim: The doctorV4FieldMapping totality rule fails on its own measurement. Two of the nineteen authorizationRecord closed members have no mapped consentRecords field, and one of them is actionSubtype, which carries the classification that FC-C5 and the CA-3 admission layer both depend on.
findings.evidence: authorizationRecord.doctorV4FieldMapping.rule reads: 'Total mapping. An authorizationRecord member with no mapped consentRecords field is a defect in this contract, not a licence to drop it.' Measured member by member: authorizationRecord.closedMembers holds nineteen names — id, actor, actionClass, actionSubtype, componentGenerationIdentity, admittedManifestDigest, designContractRef, invocationId, checkIds, resourceScope, toolIdentity, endpointSet, platform, consentCarrier, policyProvenance, productAdmissionRefs, resolution, owners, auditIdentity — and closedMemberCount 19 agrees with that count. doctorV4FieldMapping carries eighteen keys besides rule. Set difference: actor and actionSubtype appear as members with no mapping entry. A third asymmetry runs the other way — effectOutcome is a mapping key but is not an authorizationRecord member, so the key set is neither a subset nor a superset of the member set. actor may be defensible by implication, since it is closed to the single value HOST-UNDER-INSTRUCTION and every record in this schema is a host record; but the rule as written admits no exemption, and a single-valued member is exactly the kind a later implementer drops. actionSubtype is not defensible. It is the member whose absence the artifact itself makes fatal: its nullWhen clause states 'A CA-3 or CA-4-HOST record with a null or unnamed subtype is UNCLASSIFIED and must resolve DENIED', failClosed FC-C5 states 'The act and subtype are classified. UNCLASSIFIED is unexercisable regardless of consent, regardless of this contract's recording, and regardless of an authorization record', and coveredActs.CA-3 hangs a distinct productAdmissionAuthority, admissionEvidenceToday and standing off each of the four subtypes. If the subtype has no declared carrier in the doctor consent record, the post-report cannot distinguish which CA-3 subtype was attempted, which is the very distinction BLK-2 exists about and which the per-subtype admission layer was added in v2 to answer. The artifact convicts itself: by its own sentence this is 'a defect in this contract'.
findings.proposedFix: Add mapping entries for actor and actionSubtype. For actionSubtype, name the consentRecords field that carries the CA-3/CA-4 subtype and state that an unmapped or unpopulated subtype resolves DENIED, matching nullWhen and FC-C5. For actor, either map it or amend the totality rule to exempt single-valued members explicitly rather than by silence. Separately, either add effectOutcome to the member list or state in the mapping that it is an outcome field carried here for completeness and is not an authorizationRecord member, so the two sets are reconciled rather than merely overlapping.

findings.claim: The sectionExtractionRule added to repair my v2 advisory does not reproduce the sectionSha256 it accompanies. Applying the rule as written yields a different digest, and because the artifact demotes the line numbers to convenience, a verifier following the authoritative mechanism would report drift where none exists.
findings.evidence: governingDecisions.D-032 pins sectionSha256 00085513a0551aded3b1996bf448c42f16265ce0a4409eb5d926108d1bd63367 and states the rule: 'From the heading line through the last non-empty content line before the next "## " heading, excluding a trailing horizontal rule. At the previous whole-file digest 54d34099… this was lines 1621-1654. Line numbers are convenience only.' Measured in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, the D-032 section boundary is: line 1652 last content line, 1653 empty, 1654 the horizontal rule, 1655 empty, 1656 the next heading. The stated rule therefore selects lines 1621-1652 — through the last non-empty content line, excluding the trailing rule — which hashes to 672e8ecf14e8bc0b9e7a7f8737bf7de6fe3f56700139d1b78190c2bcb7c588b2. The claimed digest reproduces only at lines 1621-1654, which INCLUDES both the blank line at 1653 and the horizontal rule at 1654 that the rule says to exclude. I confirmed this two ways: an awk pipeline implementing the stated rule, and an explicit sed range, both returning 672e8ecf…, against the sed range 1621-1654 returning the claimed 00085513…. The pin itself is honest and the bytes are real — I verified the section is unchanged despite COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md moving from 54d34099… to 7c6d8a56… on the D-037 adoption, because D-037 was appended at line 1689, after D-032 and D-036. The defect is confined to the extraction rule. It matters because the artifact says line numbers are convenience only, making the rule the authoritative mechanism; a later verifier following it gets a mismatch and, under this corpus's stop-on-conflict discipline, would be obliged to treat an unchanged section as drifted.
findings.proposedFix: Restate the rule to match the bytes: 'From the heading line through the horizontal rule that terminates the section, inclusive of the intervening blank line' — or re-pin the digest to the range the current rule selects, 1621-1652 at 672e8ecf…. Either is correct; they must simply agree.

findings.claim: UNEMITTED-CRASH is introduced as a state term in prose with no definition and no home in any of the artifact's closed vocabularies, in a document that otherwise defines every closed value it uses.
findings.evidence: The token occurs twice, both consistently: effectCommit.processDeath — 'when none exists the attempt is UNEMITTED-CRASH and the fixture cannot be claimed to pass' — and the FC-PROCESS-DEATH-INDETERMINATE pass property — 'When no surviving writer exists, the fixture cannot be claimed to pass; the attempt is UNEMITTED-CRASH.' It is used coherently and it is not smuggled into the outcome vocabulary: outcomeVocabulary remains closed: true with memberCount 3 and members COMPLETED, DEFINITELY_NOT_PERFORMED, INDETERMINATE, and UNEMITTED-CRASH is a state of the attempt rather than an effectOutcome value, so the closure holds. But the artifact defines its other vocabularies explicitly — outcome members carry a meaning, and actor, actionClass and resolution carry closedValues — while this term carries neither definition nor a stated carrier. In a contract whose discipline is that a state must have a home and a writer, a state introduced only in prose is the shape the corpus's honesty rules exist to catch, even where the usage is honest.
findings.proposedFix: Give UNEMITTED-CRASH a one-line definition and say where it lives — whether it is a report-integrity state owned by the future crash-report surface, an absence recorded by the supervisor, or purely a review-side label for a fixture that cannot be claimed. If it has no carrier until that surface is owned, say so, which is consistent with the bounded obligation already recorded.

predecessorFindingVerification.IR-HEA2-A1: REPAIRED — verbatim to my proposed fix, both halves. doctorV4ReservedPoint now reads '…DR-105's closure conditions the component half of the member; under D-032 Option B host acts are outside DR-105, so the host half does not wait on DR-105. doctor v4's unpopulated-plus-residual interim rule continues to govern component records and host records made before this contract is recorded.' The first sentence disposes the conjunct v2 named and left hanging; the second preserves v4's interim rule for the cases this contract does not reach, which was the other half of my concern.
predecessorFindingVerification.IR-HEA2-A2: PARTIALLY REPAIRED. The mechanism I asked for exists — governingDecisions.D-032.sectionExtractionRule — and it is stated in terms of delimiters with line numbers demoted to convenience, exactly the form I proposed. predecessorFindingVerification.HAE2-CX-01: REPAIRED (repair present; original finding text unseen). The review prompt names the axis as CA-1 records replayable across generations and manifests. v3 adds componentGenerationIdentity — 'the exact component generation identity that will be spawned. Absent, wildcard, or mismatch with the bytes actually spawned DENIES' — admittedManifestDigest — 'sha256 of the admitted manifest of that generation. Absent or mismatch DENIES' — and designContractRef — 'A stale, moved, or unrecorded ref DENIES. Existence of this JSON on disk is not a lawful ref.' Two fixture classes, FC-CROSS-GENERATION-REPLAY and FC-WRONG-MANIFEST, test the replay case directly. The doctorV4FieldMapping half of the cited repair location is where I found the blocker.
predecessorFindingVerification.HAE2-CX-02: REPAIRED (repair present; original finding text unseen), and the second half is refused honestly rather than repaired, which I count as the correct disposition. The CA-1 commit boundary is now 'The operating system has accepted creation of the child process (the irreversible process-creation acceptance), not the parent's later observation of a pid', with unknownAcceptance covering 'cancel or parent death during the syscall and the case where a child exists before the parent call returns' and making DEFINITELY_NOT_PERFORMED unlawful in that race. whichProcessDeathEndsAuthorization answers which death matters: 'The host/doctor process that holds the authorization record. Component or tool death does not end host authorization.' The no-surviving-writer problem is not solved and is not pretended to be: processDeath states 'If doctor itself dies, doctor cannot write the post-report… No such supervisor is minted here. The missing crash-report surface is UNOWNED-AND-NEEDED; owner assignment is a D-000 act', and FC-PROCESS-DEATH-INDETERMINATE is expressly bounded — required only when a surviving writer exists — with 'That bound is not a waiver of honesty; it is a refusal to claim a report that cannot be written.' That is the honest refusal the prompt allows.
predecessorFindingVerification.HAE2-CX-03: REPAIRED (repair present; original finding text unseen), and this is the sharpest substantive fix in v3. v2's ES-2 assigned every socket opened by any process doctor spawned — 'CA-1 component or CA-2 customer tool' — to DR-105 / PT-NET-EGRESS, which mis-assigns a customer tool's egress to a component permission token. v3 splits it: ES-2a keeps admitted-component egress at DR-105 / PT-NET-EGRESS, and ES-2b states 'every network send or receive by a CA-2 customer-owned tool is not an admitted-component act and is not PT-NET-EGRESS. A customer tool is not made a component by being spawned. This contract cannot authorize those sockets. Host CA-4 never authorizes the tool's own sockets.' A PATH-SPAWNED-TOOL-EGRESS entry and an FC-HOST-CA4-NOT-TOOL fixture class carry it.
predecessorFindingVerification.HAE-CX-01..05, HAE-ADV-01 (v1 Codex): Recorded REPAIRED in predecessorVerdictFindings.v1.codex with locations. I have never read the Codex v1 or v2 verdicts. I verified the repairs at the cited locations exist and are responsive to the axes the prompt names; I cannot certify they discharge findings whose wording I have not seen.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 645eea61f9ad415cbbc75eb85a1896d7f46421a8231c5ba403b39d6b81051a8f both times. No drift.

CA-1 record is no longer replayable across generations or manifests: componentGenerationIdentity and admittedManifestDigest are both required, both DENY on absence or mismatch, and designContractRef DENIES on a stale, moved or unrecorded ref with the self-bootstrapping case named. FC-CROSS-GENERATION-REPLAY tests a GRANTED CA-1 record bound to one generation and manifest against another.

CA-1 commit is no longer parent-pid observation: the boundary is OS acceptance of process creation, stated as 'not the parent's later observation of a pid', with the ambiguous-acceptance race resolved to INDETERMINATE and DEFINITELY_NOT_PERFORMED made unlawful in it.

Process-death INDETERMINATE with no surviving writer is refused honestly, not claimed. The missing surface is named UNOWNED-AND-NEEDED, the owner-assignment route is a D-000 act for the two named owner groups, and the fixture obligation is explicitly bounded rather than asserted to pass.
CA-2 tool egress is no longer assigned to PT-NET-EGRESS. ES-2 is split and ES-2b denies both routes for a customer tool's own sockets — not a component permission, and not host CA-4.

Mapping into doctor v4 consentRecords now exists as doctorV4FieldMapping with a stated totality rule. Its completeness is where the blocker lies; the mapping's presence and its rule are otherwise exactly what the axis asked for.
The unless-bypass remains absent: coveredActs.CA-4-host carries no unless clause and thisContractCannotAdmit true, and ES-3 states 'No unless-bypass exists' for the unclassified socket.

Fail-closed remains a conjunction: 'exercisable iff FC-C1 AND FC-C2 AND FC-C3 AND FC-C4 AND FC-C5 AND FC-C6. Absence of any conjunct denies', with FC-C1 forbidding self-bootstrapping and FC-C4 forbidding this contract from standing as its own product admission.
No silent SATISFIED: the token occurs twice, both negative, in authorityClaim and whatThisDoesNotDo. Header carries CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, DO-NOT-SEAL, binds NOTHING.

No minted PT token: 'PT-' occurs ten times, of which eight are PT-NET-EGRESS and the remaining two are the literal wildcard inside the disclaimer that no PT-* token is minted. No other concrete token appears. 'WAIV' occurs zero times.

No waived join blocker: joinBlockerDisposition retains all seven with BLK-1 through BLK-4 STILL-ROUTED, BLK-3 still stating that the vocabulary's existence does not discharge it, and whatThisDoesNotDo repeating the non-discharge.

KEYCHAIN remains fail-closed: authorizationRoute DR-108, productAdmissionAuthority the DR-108 owner, admissionEvidenceToday DEFERRED, standing 'Unexercisable while DR-108 is deferred', thisContractCannotAdmit true, with D-002's explicit deferral cited as the slice selector.

No circular D-032 egress deferral: slice1EgressExecutionSide still opens by quoting the assignment and stating 'This artifact is that contract. The assignment is answered here. It is not returned UNSETTLED', and the settled rule plus ES-1/ES-2a/ES-2b/ES-3 apply it.

Recited counts: closedMemberCount 19 matches nineteen listed members; outcomeVocabulary memberCount 3 matches three listed and D-032's three; CA-3 subtypeCount 4 matches four listed and BLK-2's four effects. The one count-adjacent failure is the totality claim at the blocker, which is a set relation rather than an arithmetic recital.

verdictNote: REJECT at one blocker, and I want the shape of it clear because it is not a substantive objection. Every technical repair in v3 survives attack: the replay binding, the commit boundary, the tool-egress split, the process-death refusal, the fail-closed conjunction, the egress assignment, KEYCHAIN, the join blockers, the token and SATISFIED sweeps. I set out to falsify the CA-1 and ES-2 repairs in particular and could not. The blocker is an internal-consistency failure the artifact itself defines as one: it declares a total mapping and is short two members, one of which carries the classification its own fail-closed conjunct FC-C5 turns on. That is two entries to fix. The first advisory is the incomplete repair of my own v2 advisory — the extraction rule and the digest it accompanies select different ranges, and since the artifact demotes line numbers to convenience, the authoritative mechanism is the one that is wrong. Both are mechanical. A v4 fixing them would, on my reading, be acceptable.
